name: ferlium
description: A small, statically-typed functional scripting language for Rust hosts. Whole-module type inference, Rust-style syntax, no ambient I/O.

paragraphs: A small, statically-typed functional scripting language for Rust hosts. Whole-module type inference, Rust-style syntax, no ambient I/O.

Created by Enlightware GmbH for use in Candli, an educational game engine that teaches children STEAM through visual programming. Ferlium powers Candli's advanced script blocks: end users write logic the game engine loads, compiles, and runs.
features: Type inference with generics. Ferlium infers generic function signatures across a whole module, so fn add(a, b) { a + b } needs no annotations. Its inference is Hindley–Milner-style with constrained types; partial…
Mutable value semantics. Values can be safely mutated with the help of a small borrow checker, without a garbage collector or explicit lifetime annotations.

Algebraic data types. Records, tuples and tagged unions can be open to additional fields or variants through row polymorphism, or closed. Independently, each can remain structural or gain nominal identity through a…
Traits and modules. Traits (type classes) support multiple parameters and associated types, while module::name and use module::; organize code.
Functional core. First-class and anonymous functions with closures, pattern matching for destructuring data, and |> pipelining for chained transformations.
